decisions.reason: The pixelation check concerns rendering quality during full-page formatting and does not change the existing full-page placement requirement.
Checking pixelation after formatting does not change image-source or thematic-suitability criteria.
The source adds a chapter-image rendering check and does not alter manuscript text or content-integrity requirements.
Image pixelation is independent of chapter-heading punctuation, capitalization, and hierarchy.
Local context resolves the images as chapter images being formatted for full-page placement, not the paperback cover.
The rendering-quality check does not affect the copyright-page publication attribution.
The source does not change the approved title text or its exclusion of the unintended newline marker.
Image pixelation during layout is unrelated to prose editing, clarity, or meaning preservation.
The source requests a concrete image-quality check rather than changing the requested publishing-process guidance.
Checking full-page images for pixelation does not change pagination or table-of-contents update rules.
The source adds a rendering-quality check but does not modify the paperback format or 6-by-9-inch trim size.
Chapter-image pixelation has no effect on required back matter or author-biography content.
